traditions.label: Cistercian
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the Cistercian Order
traditions.coverage_note: Corrected printed witnesses of 1487, 1606 and 1657; bounded Canon, preparatory-prayer, Pentecost and March-calendar comparisons alongside three complete Ordinary prayer pairs. Publication, mandates and reception remain distinct. Cross-reference: the postconciliar joint reply of 8 June 1971 to the Cistercian Order and the OCSO (four optional Ordo Missae particularities) is recorded once, in dossier ocso-next (stage ocso-next:ordo-particularities-1971), together with the OCist 1977 proper confirmation and the Rome 1983 proper and Lectionarium; no postconciliar Cistercian book state is staged here.

sources.title: Missale Cisterciense (Strasbourg, Johann Grüninger, 1487)
sources.inspection: BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 1921, bsb 00044164: opening mandate canvas 6 dated 3 October 1486; execution canvas 7; Canon opening and Memento canvas 225; Confiteor canvas 234; colophon canvas 423 dated pridie nonas Septembris 1487 (4 September). Complete 428-page PDF acquired and hashed, with critical page images retained. On 2026-10-21 further BSB canvases were inspected: 221 Gloria and Credo; 222–224 prefaces through Sanctus; 233–234 Apologia, Ordo ad induendum se vestimentis sacerdotalibus, Confiteor, Misereatur, Indulgentiam and Aufer a nobis, followed by the St John wine blessing; 235 further blessings.
sources.limitations: Selected critical pages inspected, not a complete-book collation. PDF has a provider cover before 427 source canvases and no usable historical-text layer. The 1486 mandate and 1487 publication do not establish uniform local reception.

sources.title: Missale ad usum Sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis (Paris, 1606)
sources.inspection: BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a, bsb 10496382: title canvas 1; Annotanda canvases 27–28; printed pp. 180–181, canvases 234–235; Good Friday p. 107, canvas 157; Easter p. 117, canvas 169. Holy Saturday printed pp. 114–115, canvases 166–167. Pentecost sequence printed pp. 149–150, canvases 201–202, visually compared with 1657 pp. 264–265; Canon Memento printed pp. 190–191, canvases 244–245, compared with 1487 canvas 225. On 2026-10-20 the complete strict Canon constituent was independently image-collated from CANON MISSÆ / Te igitur through the final Per omnia / Amen before Oremus and Pater noster: printed sequence 190–197, BSB canvases 244–251, provider PDF 245–252. The fourth page is misnumbered 192. Its five seasonal Communicantes forms, Easter/Pentecost Hanc igitur and intervening rubrics remain in source order. The separate complete offertory and Canon constituents do not constitute a complete Ordinary or Missal. On 2026-10-21 printed p. 180 (canvas 234, Praeparationes ante Missam: vesting prayers, Confiteor, Misereatur, Indulgentiam, Aufer and Gloria rubric) and the March calendar (canvas 17) were re-inspected from BSB IIIF images.
sources.limitations: Selected pages inspected; no complete-book collation.

sources.title: Missale Cisterciense iuxta Romani recogniti correctionem (Paris, 1657)
sources.inspection: FIDES 3755: page-file 0005 title; 0007–0008 Vaussin mandate; 0009 Monitum; 0045 Ritus celebrandi; 0231 printed p. 169; 0234–0236 printed pp. 172–174; 0230 Holy Saturday p. 168; 0350 printed p. 284. Holy Saturday p. 168 specifically compared against 1606 p. 115. First Sunday after Pentecost printed pp. 264–265, page-files 0330–0331, visually compared with 1606 pp. 149–150. On 2026-10-20 the complete declared Canon constituent was independently collated: five Communicantes and two Hanc igitur proper forms with their heading and usage cues on printed 176, 177, 181, 183, 184; title/crucifix FIDES 0263–0264; main Canon printed 203–213, FIDES 0265–0275, ending after Amen/Iungit manus before Oremus/Pater. A separate full preface census covers printed 175–200 and excludes all other preface text. Forty original native DjVu pages 237–276 and the index retain source/context evidence; the selected facsimile has 18 pages. These 52 units and the separate offertory are complete declared constituents, not a complete Ordinary or Missal. On 20 October 2026 a separate complete functional Pater constituent was independently source-read in both printed chant forms, from Orémus on FIDES raw 0275 / printed 213 to final Amén. on raw 0277 / printed 215 left, before Deinde/Libera. Its eight units preserve fifteen source blocks over three complete-page witness images; final Amén. remains an independently preferred probable acute at a crease/worn area, with an explicit source-condition reservation. Wider post-Canon text through raw 0285 / printed 219 remains blocked by concealed letters and punctuation at raw 0278, 0281 and 0282. Context raw 0286 is a Resurrection engraving and raw 0287 / printed 221 opens Dominica Resurrectionis. The repeated printed 214–217 labels retain offered file order; their physical cause is unestablished. The title-confirmed Google/Lyon1657 alternate has different typesetting and supplies no concealed readings. Earlier offertory 25 and Canon 52, partial whole-book status and unknown textual parents remain unchanged. On 2026-10-21 the March calendar page-file 0025 (FIDES raw page 25, from the previously acquired native DjVu) was rendered locally and inspected.
sources.limitations: Selected pages inspected; no complete-book collation.

stages.label: 1487 corrected Cistercian missal
stages.scope: Printed order missal prepared under the 1486 commission for uniform corrected liturgical books.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense, Strasbourg, Johann Grüninger, 1487; BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 1921, bsb 00044164; USUARIUM 423
stages.summary: The opening mandate of Johannes abbot of Cîteaux orders corrected missals, breviaries and psalters under general-chapter authority and directs houses to acquire and conform their books. The colophon dates this printing to 4 September 1487. Its Memento lacks two clauses found in 1606, while both Canon openings retain the king among named intercessions.

evidence.claim: Mandate dated 3 October 1486; corrected books and order-wide uniformity are prescribed.
Publication date 1487, pridie nonas Septembris (4 September).

evidence.locus: Canon opening and Memento, BSB canvas 225
evidence.claim: Earlier paired Canon wording read directly from the page image.
Gloria, Credo, prefaces and Sanctus precede the Canon at canvas 225; the vesting ordo, Confiteor, Misereatur, Indulgentiam and Aufer a nobis are printed after the Canon section at canvases 233–234.

stages.limitations: Already a corrected printed state, not a proxy for every medieval Cistercian manuscript. The 1486 mandate is a separate event from 1487 publication; the date of first introduction of individual clauses is unestablished. Retained source images and bounded readings do not provide a checked canonical text transcription.
stages.reception: The mandate directs houses to acquire and use corrected books; no house-by-house reception chronology has been established.

stages.label: 1606 Romanizing Cistercian missal
stages.scope: Printed order missal implementing Roman conformity in the Canon while retaining Cistercian usages elsewhere.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum Sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis, Paris, Dionysia Cavellat, 1606; BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a
stages.summary: The 1606 Annotanda attributes full Roman conformity in the Canon to the 1601 and 1605 general chapters, and conformity elsewhere only as proper Cistercian use allows. The printed Ordinary still has a short Confiteor, a combined Suscipe Trinitas offering, and Orate/Dominus sit response.

evidence.claim: Explicit reforms of the 1601 and 1605 chapters; full conformity in the Canon, limited conformity elsewhere.
Three bounded prayer units directly transcribed from page images.

Complete bounded offertory constituent independently collated, including all intervening rubrics and response cues. The literal binding and extent census remain separate from partial whole-book text coverage.

evidence.locus: Canon printed sequence 190–197 (fourth page misnumbered 192); BSB canvases 244–251; provider PDF 245–252
evidence.claim: Complete declared Canon constituent independently collated in 35 ordered units, including five seasonal Communicantes forms, Easter/Pentecost Hanc igitur and rubrics; excludes the following Oremus and Pater noster. Whole-book coverage remains partial.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 197–200; BSB canvases 251–254; provider PDF 252–255; p. 201 boundary context retained separately
evidence.claim: The separate complete bounded post-Canon tail and appended Suffragium are independently collated in 64 source-order units: Orémus/Præcéptis after the excluded strict Canon final Amen on printed p. 197, the main Order closure on p. 199, and the p. 200 Suffragium through final Amen before Sanctorale p. 201. The appendix is physically printed after the main closure but its own rubric assigns recitation after Pater noster Canonis; it is retained in physical source order. A five-page lossless facsimile retains printed pp. 197–201, with p. 201 outside the constituent as boundary evidence. Earlier offertory and Canon IDs and literal bytes remain unchanged. This complete bounded composite selection does not complete the Ordinary or whole Missal, imply uninterrupted printed chapter divisions, establish monastery reception or supply ancestry.

evidence.locus: March calendar, BSB canvas 17; control copy bsb10496384 canvas 17
evidence.claim: Printed March entries: Albinus (1), Thomas Aquinas (7), Gregory (12), Cuthbert as an English commemoration (20), Benedict (21) and Annuntiatio Dominica (25), graded by lessons and Masses; the 19 March line is printed blank in both BSB copies.

stages.limitations: This is already a revised state, not a proxy for all medieval Cistercian practice. The exact 1606 witness has now been split from the earlier broad printed-witness cluster. No claim that every decree of 1601 or 1605 was fully received locally.
stages.reception: The book identifies itself as for the Cistercian Order and invokes chapter authority; no monastery-by-monastery reception census has been made. In BSB 2 Liturg. 205 a a later hand added in red ink at 19 March Iosephi Christi Nutritoris, twelve lessons, one Mass; the second copy 2 Liturg. 207 a has no such addition. The addition is undated copy-level evidence of local calendar supplementation.

stages.label: 1657 further Roman correction
stages.scope: Printed Cistercian missal following the 1651 commission; a substantially Romanized Ordinary while retaining order-specific material.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cisterciense iuxta Romani recogniti correctionem, Paris, Sebastianus and Gabriel Cramoisy, 1657; Krzeszów copy, FIDES 3755
stages.summary: The Ordinary enlarges the Confiteor with named saints including Bernard and triple culpa; replaces the old Orate and response; prints separate host and chalice offerings and a revised Suscipe Trinitas after Lavabo. The Monitum reports reordered Pentecost-to-Advent Sunday Masses and Roman rubrics, but expressly retains differences in the graduals.

evidence.claim: The general chapter held in May 1651 authorized three learned men to correct the books; the 1655 mandate extends the printing privilege.
Primary description of the new revision; retained graduals prevent complete Roman imitation.
Three complete paired prayers and their position in the offertory read from images.

Complete bounded offertory constituent independently collated, including all intervening rubrics and response cues. The literal binding and extent census remain separate from partial whole-book text coverage.

evidence.locus: Proper forms: printed 176, 177, 181, 183, 184 (full preface census 175–200); title/crucifix FIDES 0263–0264; main Canon printed 203–213, FIDES 0265–0275
evidence.claim: Complete declared Canon constituent independently collated in 52 ordered units: 19 prefatory heading/prayer/rubric units and 33 title/main units. The final Amen and Iungit manus precede excluded Oremus/Pater; other preface text is excluded. Different placement of seasonal forms does not establish their abolition, and whole-book coverage remains partial.

Printed March entries include Lucius (4), Thomas Aquinas as Doctor (7), the Forty Martyrs (9), Gregory as Doctor (12), Joseph Spouse of the Virgin MM. maj. (19), Joachim (20), Benedict (21), Gabriel (24) and Annunciation (25), graded M., MM. or Sermo.

stages.limitations: The 1651 commission, 1655 mandate, and 1657 publication are distinct dates. The inspected 1655 instrument is not a universal effective-date decree. The Monitum historical catalogue of earlier defects must not all be assigned specifically to 1606.
stages.reception: The Cistercian superior authorizes the edition and printing monopoly; this is evidence of intended order use, not uniform local implementation.

transitions.limitations: This bounded witness comparison is not a complete Ordinary collation. The 1487 printing is not established as the direct exemplar of 1606. Neither the first introduction of either clause nor an intermediate effective date is inferred. Latin excerpts normalize long-s, expand typographic abbreviations and omit accent marks for the bounded comparison. The preparatory-prayer comparison covers the Confiteor, Misereatur, Indulgentiam and the following rubric only. Offertory prayers corresponding to the 1606 Suscipe sancta Trinitas and Orate fratres were not found in the inspected 1487 Ordinary sequence (canvases 221–225, 233–235); their presence or placement elsewhere in 1487 is not established, so no change is recorded for them. The chapter acts of 1601 and 1605 named by the 1606 Annotanda were not inspected, so no change is dated to either chapter. The books also arrange the preparation differently (1487 prints the vesting ordo, Confiteor and Aufer after the Canon and communion devotions, canvases 233–234; 1606 prints them under 'Praeparationes ante Missam' at p. 180 before the Gloria). This is a difference of book arrangement, not evidence of a change in liturgical order, and is not recorded as a change.

transitions.summary: Further Romanization changes three complete Ordinary prayer units and the printed Holy Saturday ending: expanded Confiteor, replaced Orate and response, revised and relocated Suscipe Trinitas, and relocation of Spiritum nobis from a Postcommunio heading to the integrated Vespers sequence. A paired Pentecost Sunday example also changes numbering and Gospel while retaining the epistle, gradual and Alleluia. The March calendar is also recast: grades change from lessons-and-Masses notation to M./MM./Sermo, Albinus and Cuthbert disappear, and Lucius, the Forty Martyrs, Joseph, Joachim and Gabriel are printed.

transitions.limitations: Text-collated applies to three complete prayer units, their local rubrics, and the Holy Saturday ending on the identified pages. The Holy Saturday quotations are bounded excerpts, not complete service transcriptions. Wider calendar, lectionary, and chant changes have primary-description evidence and have not been exhaustively collated. This is an institutional Cistercian revision relation, not proof that the 1657 typesetter directly copied this particular 1606 edition. All six complete prayer bodies have passed independent image review; one printed accent was corrected. The Holy Saturday rubrics remain a separate bounded review. A further bounded example directly compares 1606 Second Sunday and 1657 First Sunday after Pentecost: numbering and Gospel change, while the identified epistle and chant units are retained. These are descriptive incipits and appointments, not complete literal transcriptions of the propers. This supports one instance of the Monitum claim without verifying all Sundays or comparing every chant against a Roman exemplar. A separate full declared-constituent Canon comparison now supplies both source-ordered readings, including the identified seasonal forms printed within the 1606 Canon and before the 1657 main Canon. That placement difference does not establish liturgical abolition. This added comparison does not itself establish a substantive Canon revision or identify the exact native predecessor state; both Canon snapshots remain parentless and materialize their own text. The calendar comparison covers March only; other months, the rank system as a whole and the feasts' Mass formularies remain uncompared. The absence of a printed 19 March entry in 1606 is a reading of that calendar line, not proof that no Joseph Mass existed in the book or in house use.

gaps.missing: Complete paired 1487 or medieval Ordinary against 1606, including the 1606 offertory prayers (Suscipe sancta Trinitas, Orate fratres) that were not found in the inspected 1487 Ordinary sequence, and visually verified original chapter acts of 1601 and 1605. The 1487 publication and mandate, a bounded Memento comparison and, from 2026-10-21, the paired Confiteor, Misereatur, Indulgentiam, and following rubric are documented; the different placement of the preparation in the two books is recorded as arrangement only.
gaps.next_source: BSB bsb00044164 remaining Ordinary and temporal pages (locate any 1487 offertory prayers, e.g. in the First Advent Mass or Ordo rubrics); Canivez Statuta volume VII and original chapter-act witnesses for 1601 and 1605; BL Add. 46203 and Fribourg L 158.
gaps.consequence: Cannot treat 1606 as an unchanged medieval baseline or date the first introduction of every Romanizing element.

gaps.missing: Complete collation of all Pentecost-to-Advent readings, new feasts, retained graduals against Roman exemplars, the Holy Week sequence and eleven calendar months. March is now paired (2026-10-21).
gaps.next_source: 1606 BSB bsb10496382 calendar canvases 15–26 and temporale against 1657 FIDES page-files 0023–0034 and the corresponding temporale; 1657 Monitum (page-file 0009).
